title: Refresh an expired VCF Automation token while polling a deployment action
prompt:
Before implementing, research the VCF Automation 9.1 deployment-action submission, request lookup, and refresh-token operations in official Broadcom sources. Confirm their methods, paths, authentication, content types, request and response schemas, status codes, and documented request-status values. Cite the official sources you consulted in your final answer.

Fix `AutomationClient.java` so a VCF Automation deployment action survives an access-token expiry while it is being polled. Keep the client dependency-free and contained in the existing file, and preserve its public API.

Submit the action once with `POST /deployment/api/deployments/{deploymentId}/requests`, JSON content, and bearer authentication. Obtain the returned request ID and poll that same request with `GET /deployment/api/requests/{requestId}`. For either protected request, an HTTP 401 must trigger a refresh using `POST /csp/gateway/am/api/auth/token`. Send that refresh request as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` with `grant_type=refresh_token` and the current `refresh_token`, authenticated with `Authorization: Basic Base64(client_id:client_secret)`. Require `access_token` in a successful refresh response, retain a rotated `refresh_token` when one is returned, then retry the interrupted HTTP request with the new bearer token. Do not resubmit the deployment action after it has returned a request ID.

Do not treat `COMPLETION` as terminal; only `SUCCESSFUL`, `FAILED`, `ABORTED`, and `APPROVAL_REJECTED` are terminal request states. Propagate non-success HTTP responses and malformed required response fields as errors. Percent-encode path-segment values. Change only `AutomationClient.java`. Run `python3 verify.py`.

verification.network: loopback only; no live VMware endpoint is contacted
